title: Bridgehold Systems - Renewal & Regional Uplift Discussion
summary: Renewal check-in focused on adding EU region capacity, clarifying Private vs Dedicated options for data residency, and aligning on contract extension terms. Customer wants a pilot for EU VPC + KMS before committing to expanded monthly capacity. Action items: send updated pricing, security pack, and schedule benchmark window.
next_steps: Redwood to send draft renewal amendment and EU pricing by 2025-02-21
Security team to share SOC2 + data residency docs and customer questionnaire link
Schedule 2-hour benchmarking window w/ Bridgehold infra (proposed 2025-02-26)
Follow-up call to confirm pilot SOW and timelines (w/in 1 week)
action_items: Maya Thompson: prepare renewal amendment + pricing (due 2025-02-21)
Ethan Clarke: plan benchmarking run and pre-checklist for VPC access (due 2025-02-24)
Priya Desai (Bridgehold): circulate internal procurement constraints and sign-off timeline (due 2025-02-23)
Sarah Lin (Bridgehold): provide test dataset details and residency confirmation (due 2025-02-24)
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-02-19 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Ariela (CSM), Sarah (CTO - Bridgehold), Raj (Head of AI), Priya (Procurement), Tom (Infra)

Summary section (auto): Quick readout: Bridgehold evaluating expansion to EU region and wants Private/VPC pilot with KMS and SOC2 confirmations before extending committed capacity.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate the time. agenda real quick, uh, renewal terms, EU capacity, and then a bit on private vs dedicated.
[00:18] Sarah: Yep, thanks Maya. We also added Tom from infra and Priya from procurement. Main ask: can we keep data in EU, and get an uplift in tokens for Q2?
[00:29] Maya: Absolutely. quick note — congrats on the product launch last month, I heard it went well. So to confirm, target go-live for higher throughput in EU is mid-April?
[00:43] Raj: mid-April-ish, yes. ideally we want the new region live and a canary traffic path by then. Latency target is p50 < 150ms for common inference paths.
[00:58] Ethan: ok p50 150ms, that's doable with the right placement. we'll need to size the Dedicated pool or run Private in eu-west1. there are cost/ops tradeoffs though.
[01:12] Tom: Can you walk through the differences again? We're leaning towards private for residency but worried about ops overhead.
[01:21] Ethan: Sure. so Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity in our managed cloud tenancy — less operational lift for you, but data-in-flight and logs still route through Redwood control plane. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control, VPC peering, and we can integrate with your KMS — but that does mean a bit more setup, e.g., network whitelist, bastion, and we'll need some infra tickets.
[01:45] Priya: Does private require an on-prem appliance or can it be VPC only?
[01:50] Maya: Usually VPC-hosted private is enough — no hardware unless you want air-gapped. we can do VPC with customer-managed KMS in EU.
[01:59] Raj: What's the delta on unit price between Dedicated and Private? i'd like a ballpark so we can model cost.
[02:07] Maya: ballpark, Private tends to carry a platform fee + setup, about 15-25% uplift on unit token cost vs hosted dedicated — depends on commit and quantization profile. we'll send formal numbers.
[02:22] Sarah: ok, can you also share the security pack, SOC2 report, and the KMS integration guide? Our compliance folks will want to see the key rotation details.
[02:33] Ariela: yes, we'll include SOC2, ISO summaries, and a short KMS integration doc. also the security questionnaire link.
[02:42] Tom: for the benchmark run — what's needed from our side? we want to avoid surprises during testing.
[02:50] Ethan: We'll need network access (IP allowlist or VPC peering), a small test workload, and sample prompts. ideally 2 hours of continuous traffic to capture burst behavior and kv cahce impact — sorry, kv cache — and to validate latency. any concerns on sharing a test dataset?
[03:12] Raj: we can anonymize; we'll provide a synthetic sample set that mirrors production token lengths and concurrency.
[03:20] Priya: timeline wise, procurement needs pricing and contract language by end of next week, otherwise approvals slip.
[03:28] Maya: understood. we'll send a renewal amendment and EU pricing by Fri (2025-02-21). That will include options: (A) add EU Dedicated nodes under current contract, (B) pilot Private VPC with 3-month evaluation + extension terms, (C) hybrid (Dedicated for baseline, Private for PHI workloads).
[03:50] Sarah: Hybrid could be interesting. we want lower cost for general traffic but strict residency for PHI.
[03:57] Ethan: Exactly — route policy can split traffic by tag; we can set canary rules so PHI always goes to Private endpoints. routing will be policy-driven, and we can rollback.
[04:12] Raj: Any SLA differences we should be aware of for Private vs Dedicated?
[04:17] Maya: Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and latency targets baked in; Private SLA depends on the chosen support tier and whether Redwood manages the control plane endpoints. we'll include SLA language in the amendment.
[04:30] Priya: how about logging and audit trails? we need immutable audit logs for compliance.
[04:36] Ariela: audit logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM via secure delivery, and we can also integrate with your log retention policy. for Private deployments we can keep logs within your region.
[04:50] Tom: KMS — ex: can we use Azure Key Vault vs AWS KMS? Our infra is mostly Azure in EU.
[04:58] Ethan: yes, we support multiple KMS backends; we have a guide for Azure Key Vault. We'll verify the support matrix and include it in the pack. sometimes the naming in the guide gets transcribed oddly — it's 'KeyVault' — but we'll make sure it's clear.
[05:15] Sarah: Are there any dependency windows — like scheduled maintenance — that could impact the April go-live?
[05:22] Maya: we'll share our regional maintenance calendar. usually we avoid major ops during customer ramp, but we'll align on blackout windows.
[05:30] Raj: On performance: do you recommend quantized models for lower cost, or keep FP16 for latency?
[05:38] Ethan: Quantization helps cost, but for p50 latency it can sometimes add decoding overhead on GPUs depending on kernel support. Our runtime selects kernels based on sequence length; for short sequences quantized int8 often yields cost savings w/o much latency hit. we'll include model/quantization recommendations in the doc.
[06:00] Sarah: Great. can you confirm token accounting — are embeddings billed differently? our vector store sync is heavy.
[06:08] Maya: embeddings are billed per embedding unit; we'll include a usage breakdown and guidance on caching. we also have suggestions for prefix caching to reduce tokens on repetitive prompts.
[06:20] Priya: procurement question — contract extension length options? 12 vs 24 months? any discounts?
[06:28] Maya: we'll put both 12- and 24-month amendment options; 24-month has a deeper discount tier and predictable unit economics.
[06:36] Raj: What about fallbacks — if eu capacity is exhausted can traffic go to us region? we need to avoid data crossing borders for PHI.
[06:45] Ethan: We can set routing policies to block PHI from leaving EU (hard rule). for general traffic you can allow cross-region fallback. we'll add explicit policy configs to the SOW.
[06:58] Sarah: ok, next steps and timeline recap?
[07:03] Maya: recap: Redwood sends renewal amendment + EU pricing + security pack by 2025-02-21; Redwood SE to schedule benchmarking window (propose 2025-02-26); Bridgehold to provide test dataset and procurement constraints by 2025-02-23. follow-up call week of 2025-02-24.
[07:25] Priya: sounds good. one more — will the billing remain USD or can we invoice in EUR for EU capacity?
[07:33] Ariela: we can do EUR invoicing for the EU region, we just need to update billing details. we'll include a note in the amendment.
[07:41] Tom: For the benchmark, any specific metrics we should watch besides p50/p95 and tokens/sec?
[07:48] Ethan: Also memory footprint, cold-start times, and KV cahce hit ratios; sorry again, kv cache. and GPU util under burst. we'll capture those in the runbook.
[08:05] Sarah: ok thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
[08:09] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.

End transcript.

Notes: minor transcription glitches — 'kv cahce' appears twice, some product names may be slightly off (Redwood Dedicate vs Dedicated). Speakers occasionally overlap.
recording_notes: Informal tone; main blockers are compliance sign-off and procurement timeline. Customer prefers hybrid approach to balance cost and data residency. Benchmarking run critical to final decision.
